chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
When the extremities (ends) of blessings reach you, do not repel their furthest (or greatest) extent through scarcity of gratitude.

key_terms.أَقْصَاهَا: its furthest extent, greatest part, or most distant benefit
key_terms.تُنَفِّرُوا: you repel, drive away, or deter

ai.seo_question: How does lack of gratitude for small favors affect greater blessings?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of 'gradual loss' (Tadarruj), warning that neglecting gratitude for minor, accessible blessings ('atraf') can cause the loss of greater, more distant ones ('aqsha'). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding that thankfulness is not merely a reaction to abundance but a spiritual mechanism that preserves and expands divine favor, linking the micro-practice of daily gratitude to the macro-outcome of sustained prosperity.
